name: io.github.2016judea/trading-harness
title: Trading Harness
description: Value a company from its SEC filings, and check your own trades, stops and rebalance math

tools.name: as_reported_financials
tools.description: A company's annual figures exactly as filed with the SEC (XBRL companyfacts, 10-K/20-F/40-F): revenue, gross profit, operating income, net income, cash from operations, capex, D&A, stock comp, dividends, buybacks, assets, liabilities, equity, cash, goodwill, intangibles, debt and diluted shares, by fiscal year, with the XBRL tag behind each line and the filing each year came from. Optionally a trailing-twelve-month column built from 10-Q year-to-date facts. Keyed on the period a fact covers, not the filing it appeared in. Examples: {"ticker": "KO"}; {"ticker": "CTVA", "years": 5, "ttm": true}.

ticker.description: US-listed ticker that files with the SEC, e.g. KO or BRK.B

tools.name: owner_earnings_valuation
tools.description: Owner earnings by year (net income + depreciation + amortisation - capex, Buffett 1986) beside free cash flow as a cross-check, return on equity and on tangible capital, and, given a share price, the owner-earnings yield against the long bond, three value anchors per share (bond-equivalent, two-stage DCF on normalised and on latest owner earnings), a margin-of-safety ladder, a reverse DCF (the owner-earnings growth the price requires at 8, 9, 10 and 12% required returns) and a growth x required-return sensitivity grid. Returns refused with a reason, and no value, when fewer than three of the last five years had positive owner earnings, the latest year was a loss, or owner earnings exceed 1.6x actual free cash flow. Inputs from SEC filings; price supplied by the caller. Examples: {"ticker": "KO", "price": 70.1}; {"ticker": "CTVA", "price": 62.5, "long_bond_pct": 5.2, "hurdle_pct": 9}; {"ticker": "DE"} (history only).

ticker.description: US-listed ticker that files with the SEC, e.g. KO or BRK.B

long_bond_pct.description: Long-bond yield in percent (5.4 = 5.4%). Default: the latest 30-year Treasury par yield, fetched from treasury.gov

shares_millions.description: Shares outstanding in millions (default: the latest count on the company's filings)

tools.name: compare_valuations
tools.description: Ranks 2 to 8 companies on the expectations gap: the owner-earnings growth each price requires (reverse DCF) minus the growth the business actually delivered over its last five fiscal years. Negative means the price asks for less than the company has already done. Per company: owner-earnings yield, return on tangible capital, ROE, gross margin first and last year, revenue and owner-earnings CAGR, the base used (latest year for a steady riser, an average for a cyclical) and a reading; refusals and do-not-extrapolate cases are labelled instead of ranked. The gap does not move with the hurdle the way absolute values do. Example: {"companies": [{"ticker": "KO", "price": 70.1}, {"ticker": "PEP", "price": 150.2}, {"ticker": "KDP", "price": 33.4}]}.

ticker.description: US-listed ticker that files with the SEC, e.g. KO or BRK.B

companies.description: Ticker and current share price for each company

long_bond_pct.description: Long-bond yield in percent (5.4 = 5.4%). Default: the latest 30-year Treasury par yield, fetched from treasury.gov

hurdle_pct.description: Required return for the reverse DCF, % (default 8)

tools.name: realized_pnl
tools.description: Realized profit and loss from a pasted transactions export: sells matched first-in-first-out against earlier buys per symbol, fees on both sides taken out of the gain. Returns win rate, net, average win and loss, payoff ratio, average holding period in calendar days, totals by symbol, the worst and best closed lots, and sells with no buy in the data (reported apart, not counted as zero-cost wins). Reads E*TRADE's transaction download, the CSV this repo's fetcher writes, or any CSV with columns date, action (buy/sell), symbol, quantity, price and optionally fee. Options rows are set aside and counted. Nothing pasted is stored. Example: {"transactions_csv": "date,action,symbol,quantity,price,fee\n2025-01-06,buy,KO,100,61.20,0\n2025-09-02,sell,KO,100,69.85,0"}.

transactions_csv.description: The transactions export as CSV text, header row included

symbol.description: Limit the result to one symbol

tools.name: stop_coverage_check
tools.description:
Compares positions with the orders actually resting at the broker. Flags: a position over the size cap with no resting stop, or a stop covering only part of it; any good-for-day order (gone at the close); resting sells exceeding shares held with no link between the legs; resting orders in names not held. With journal text in this repo's JOURNAL.template.md format, it also checks each written price gate (stops, sell limits, dated exits) against the resting orders and lists any gate it could not read as UNCHECKED rather than passing. Positions: symbol, quantity, and market value or last price. Orders: symbol, side, quantity, order type, limit price, stop price, term (GTC/day), status; the text "none" means no open orders. Nothing pasted is stored. Example: {"positions_csv": "symbol,quantity,last_price
KO,200,70.10
AAPL,120,229.80", "orders_csv": "symbol,side,quantity,order_type,stop_price,term
KO,sell,200,stop,62,GTC", "cap_pct": 25}.

positions_csv.description: Positions export as CSV text, header row included

orders_csv.description: Open orders as CSV text, or "none"

journal_text.description: Optional trading journal in this repo's template format

cap_pct.description: Position size, % of the account, above which a stop is expected (default 28)

cash.description: Cash in the account, for position weights (default: a cash row in the export, else 0)

tools.name: rebalance_order_list
tools.description: The dollar and share change per name to move a pasted positions export to target weights, as a list. Weights are a share of investable capital (positions + cash on hand - cash reserve). Each row: current $ and %, target %, dollar change, shares at the last price, direction, and whether exiting it would realize a gain or harvest a loss (from unrealized P&L; holding periods are not in a positions export, so short- vs long-term is not known). A target with no holding and no price is sized in dollars only. Arithmetic only: no order is placed or previewed. Nothing pasted is stored. Example: {"positions_csv": "symbol,quantity,last_price,total_gain\nAAPL,120,229.80,5940\nKO,200,70.10,-210", "target_weights_pct": {"AAPL": 30, "KO": 30, "VTI": 40}, "cash_on_hand": 10000, "prices": {"VTI": 301.55}}.

positions_csv.description: Positions export as CSV text, header row included

target_weights_pct.description: Symbol -> target weight in percent (30 = 30%); 0 is a full exit

cash_on_hand.description: Uninvested cash (default: a cash row in the export, else 0)

cash_reserve.description: Cash to keep out of the allocation (default 0)

prices.description: Symbol -> price, for targets not currently held

sell_unlisted.description: Also exit held names absent from the targets (default false)

tools.name: is_this_stock_undervalued
tools.description: Whether a company's share price sits above or below what its owner earnings support, from its SEC filings: value per share on three anchors, the price's gap to each, a margin-of-safety ladder, and the growth the price requires. Same engine as owner_earnings_valuation. Returns refused, with the reason, when the business has no durable owner earnings to value. Example questions: "Is Coca-Cola undervalued at $70?"; "What's Deere's intrinsic value?"; "Is MSFT overvalued right now?"

ticker.description: US-listed ticker that files with the SEC, e.g. KO or BRK.B

long_bond_pct.description: Long-bond yield in percent (5.4 = 5.4%). Default: the latest 30-year Treasury par yield, fetched from treasury.gov

tools.name: growth_priced_into_stock
tools.description: The owner-earnings growth a share price requires over 10 years (a reverse DCF) at 8, 9, 10 and 12% required returns, from the company's SEC filings, followed by the full owner-earnings valuation. The reading that does not depend on a chosen hurdle rate. Example questions: "What growth is priced into Nvidia?"; "What does the market expect from Costco at $900?"; "Reverse DCF on KO"

ticker.description: US-listed ticker that files with the SEC, e.g. KO or BRK.B

long_bond_pct.description: Long-bond yield in percent (5.4 = 5.4%). Default: the latest 30-year Treasury par yield, fetched from treasury.gov

tools.name: which_stock_is_cheapest
tools.description: Ranks two or more companies by the gap between price and owner-earnings value, from their SEC filings, with the loss-makers and the unvaluable named rather than dropped. Same engine as compare_valuations. Example questions: "Which is cheaper, Coke or Pepsi?"; "Rank AAPL, MSFT and GOOGL on value"; "Which of my stocks is most overvalued?"

ticker.description: US-listed ticker that files with the SEC, e.g. KO or BRK.B

companies.description: Ticker and current share price for each company

tools.name: free_cash_flow_history
tools.description: A company's free cash flow by fiscal year (operating cash flow minus capital expenditure) with both inputs, as reported on its annual SEC filings, plus the filing links. Example questions: "What's Apple's free cash flow?"; "Has Ford's free cash flow grown?"; "10 years of FCF for COST"

ticker.description: US-listed ticker that files with the SEC, e.g. KO or BRK.B

tools.name: dividends_and_buybacks
tools.description: Cash a company returned to shareholders by fiscal year, dividends paid and shares repurchased, beside its free cash flow, as reported on its annual SEC filings. Example questions: "How much does Apple spend on buybacks?"; "Can Verizon cover its dividend?"; "Dividend history for KO"

ticker.description: US-listed ticker that files with the SEC, e.g. KO or BRK.B

tools.name: short_vs_long_term_capital_gains
tools.description: Realized gains and losses from a pasted broker transactions export, split into short-term (held a year or less) and long-term by tax year, lots matched first-in, first-out, with sells that have no buy in the export set aside. Example questions: "How much short-term gain did I have this year?"; "Split my 2025 trades into short and long term"; "What are my capital gains?"

transactions_csv.description: The transactions or gains/losses CSV from the broker, pasted as text (E*TRADE download, this repo's CSV, or plain columns date, action, symbol, quantity, price, fee)

tax_year.description: One tax year (default: every year in the export)

tools.name: wash_sale_check
tools.description: Screens a pasted broker transactions export for losing sales with the same ticker bought within 30 days before or after, listing each sale, its loss and the repurchases. Example questions: "Did I trigger any wash sales?"; "Is my TSLA loss a wash sale?"; "Check my trades for the 30-day rule"

transactions_csv.description: The transactions or gains/losses CSV from the broker, pasted as text (E*TRADE download, this repo's CSV, or plain columns date, action, symbol, quantity, price, fee)

tools.name: tax_loss_harvest_candidates
tools.description: Positions sitting at an unrealized loss in a pasted positions export, largest loss first, with the total; given a transactions export too, flags any bought in the last 30 days (wash-sale risk on a sale). Example questions: "What can I tax-loss harvest?"; "Which of my positions are losers?"; "Any losses to offset my gains this year?"

positions_csv.description: The positions/portfolio CSV from the broker, pasted as text (symbol, quantity, market value or last price; a gain or cost-basis column for gains and losses)

transactions_csv.description: The transactions or gains/losses CSV from the broker, pasted as text (E*TRADE download, this repo's CSV, or plain columns date, action, symbol, quantity, price, fee). Optional: flags recent buys for the 30-day rule

tools.name: trading_win_rate
tools.description: Win rate, average win, average loss, payoff ratio and average hold from a pasted broker transactions export, with the best and worst trades and the totals by symbol. Same engine as realized_pnl. Example questions: "What's my win rate?"; "Am I a good trader?"; "What were my worst trades this year?"

transactions_csv.description: The transactions or gains/losses CSV from the broker, pasted as text (E*TRADE download, this repo's CSV, or plain columns date, action, symbol, quantity, price, fee)

tools.name: positions_without_stop_loss
tools.description: Which held positions have no working stop order covering them, from pasted positions and open-orders exports: each row critical, warning, ok or unchecked, with the reason. Same engine as stop_coverage_check. Example questions: "Do all my positions have stop losses?"; "Which stocks am I holding with no stop?"; "Did my stop orders expire?"

positions_csv.description: The positions/portfolio CSV from the broker, pasted as text (symbol, quantity, market value or last price; a gain or cost-basis column for gains and losses)

orders_csv.description: Open orders as CSV text, or "none"
